question: Does breathing drive heart rate at rest, and can Dynamic Resonance Rooting recover that respiratory sinus arrhythmia coupling from real recordings?

literature.search: respiratory sinus arrhythmia or cardiorespiratory coupling

preregistration.title: Does DRR recover respiration-to-heart-rate coupling (RSA) in resting young adults?
preregistration.question: Can DRR's surrogate-tested lead-lag analysis detect the well-established coupling from respiration to heart rate in real resting recordings, while not detecting it between different people?
preregistration.hypothesis: In at least 80% of 10-minute resting recordings from healthy young adults (PhysioNet Fantasia), DRR detects respiration -> heart-rate coupling (max-statistic adjusted p <= 0.05, lags 0.25-3 s), given that mismatched-subject pairs are detected in at most 25% and the synthetic controls behave as calibrated.
preregistration.rationale: External real-data validation for DRR, whose only prior external test (QBO) was not supported. Respiratory sinus arrhythmia is established physiology, so this is a positive control on real recordings: a sound lead-lag method must find it in matched pairs and must not find it between mismatched subjects, whose breathing and heart rate share a ~0.25 Hz rhythm but no causal link. Literature context comes from Anna (arXiv) and the R.A.I.N. panel; criteria were fixed before any coupling statistic was computed on real data.
procedure: Retrieve and cite literature with Anna; seal the anna-research-record/v1 and re-verify every excerpt against the index.
Convene the R.A.I.N. offline panel over Anna's sources and archive the transcript.
Pre-register this definition in the R.A.I.N. registry before any data is fetched.
Fetch seconds 60-660 of each listed Fantasia record by HTTP byte range; hash every byte.
Detect R peaks (5-20 Hz band-pass, 330 ms refractory); exclude records whose valid-RR fraction is below 0.95.
Resample respiration (1 Hz low-pass) and instantaneous heart rate onto a 4 Hz grid; high-pass both at 0.05 Hz; z-score.
Run DRR RootingAnalyzer (lagged correlation, lags 1-12 samples, 199 circular-shift surrogates, max-statistic correction) on each subject's [respiration, heart rate].
Run the identical test on mismatched pairs (respiration of subject i, heart rate of subject i+1) and on 20 synthetic directed and 20 synthetic independent AR(1) pairs.
Submit measurements as rain-experiment-submission/v1; R.A.I.N. evaluates the criteria.

independent: pairing: same subject vs mismatched subject
dependent: max-statistic adjusted p-value, respiration -> heart rate
lag of the strongest lagged correlation
controls: identical preprocessing, lag window, surrogates and correction for every pair

metrics.name: records_analyzed
metrics.description: Records that passed R-peak QC and were analyzed.

metrics.name: coupling_detection_rate
metrics.description: Share of analyzed records with respiration -> heart-rate adjusted p <= alpha.

metrics.name: mismatched_detection_rate
metrics.description: Share of mismatched-subject pairs with adjusted p <= alpha.

metrics.name: positive_control_detection_rate
metrics.description: Share of synthetic directed pairs detected.

metrics.name: synthetic_null_false_positive_rate
metrics.description: Share of independent synthetic pairs falsely detected.

metrics.name: reverse_detection_rate
metrics.description: Share of records with heart rate -> respiration adjusted p <= alpha (descriptive; direction is not claimed).

metrics.name: median_coupling_lag_s
metrics.description: Median lag of detected respiration -> heart-rate couplings (descriptive).

metrics.name: spectral_peak_agreement_rate
metrics.description: Share of records whose dominant Welch peaks of respiration and heart rate agree within 0.03 Hz (descriptive).

metrics.name: median_heart_rate_bpm
metrics.description: Median of per-record mean heart rate (descriptive).

guards.note: At most 4 of 20 records may fail QC.
The test must have power on a known coupling.
The test must stay near its nominal 5% false-alarm rate.
Shared rhythm alone must not produce detections; otherwise no conclusion.

limitations: Lagged correlation ignores sign and lag 0, and respiration and heart rate share one rhythm, so the reverse direction may score as high: this tests coupling, not direction.
Fantasia subjects are healthy young adults in supine rest watching the film Fantasia; nothing here generalizes to other ages, conditions or postures.
R peaks come from a simple band-pass detector; records below the QC threshold are excluded, not repaired.
Respiratory sinus arrhythmia is established physiology; this experiment tests whether DRR recovers it, not whether it exists.
Literature retrieval uses Anna's deterministic hashing embeddings (lexical, not semantic) over arXiv metadata and abstracts only.
